comments.author: @GospelProgressionsUniversity
comments.text:
Some people criticize AI-generated content just because it’s made by AI and get hung-up on that forgetting that audiences usually know it’s artificial. Most creators using AI aren’t trying to fool anyone into believing their work is “real.” The goal is to create an engaging experience and a compelling result.

Think of a haunted house on Halloween. everyone knows it’s fake. They know the ghouls and zombies aren’t real, and no one’s actually trying to eat their brains. Yet they still go back every year because it’s fun and immersive.

We’re reaching a point where the tools (like AI) matter less than the creative experiences and outcomes built with them.

comments.text:
Unimaginative and dumb. Just another desperate cash grab for half baked ideas that future AI tools will make completely obsolete.

Anyone thinking the future of content is going to be human beings using AI to create videos that we scroll through, doesn't understand AI and is ill-prepared for the future it will bring. Congratulations You made a video and got some views and advertising revenue. What did you do to actually benefit the human species? You think in 2 to 3 years people are going to give a crap about how you used AI to create videos when a basic prompt to an AI can generate an entire movie of higher caliber than the most expensive productions in today's world?

The projects that these text video AI tools will help create which will actually matter, the ones that help disseminate profound and very useful ideas throughout society that previously had been suppressed and couldn't be brought to large audiences in a high quality format because movie studios and other media interests invest in the lowest common denominator. When you produce content with these tools that continues to invest in going viral based upon tailoring to the lowest common denominator, you perpetuate a broken system that says you don't understand where the value of this tool is. That you're still stuck in the old outmoded cycle of just trying to get some money for no other reason than get money. What's the point in accruing wealth if you don't actually do something useful with it. And no I don't think a person's ongoing survival is all that useful if all they're doing is creating videos that go viral to make profit.
